transcript: If you're like me and missed A Case for The Existence of God at Signature a few years back, this is your sign to make haste and book a ticket to see Grangeville, another two hander by Samuel D. Hunter making its premiere at Signature. I loved this play. It’s 90 melancholic but engrossing minutes following a pair of half brothers as they work through old wounds and present troubles under the backdrop of their mother being her final stage of life. I don't think this is the kind of show that'll be everyone's cup of tea — I can see some describing it as slow, but I'd argue that there's a lot going on in this piece, especially as a character study. You're just a fly on the wall to a pair of people existing in a simple but beautifully and delicately crafted set of personal circumstances, so if that interests you, I cannot recommend this enough. At least the audience that I was a part of was very locked in, and with it being a matinee, I think that's a pretty strong testimony for how captivating this was. With that, another program for my collection.
